topic.title: Possible one-electron offset in positive-mode m/z
topic.forumName: Enveda CASMI 2026 - Molecule ID From Mass Spectra
topic.content:
In the Enveda-180 processing code, the positive-mode m/z calibrants are sodium formate clusters built as SOME_POLYMER_UNIT_MZ * num + SODIUM_MAYBE_MZ (calibration.py, line 45), with SODIUM_MAYBE_MZ = 22.989769 (line 14).

That is the mass of the neutral Na atom (NIST). Subtracting one electron (0.55 mDa, CODATA) gives Na⁺ = 22.989221 Da, so every positive cluster reference is 0.55 mDa too heavy. The negative-mode clusters use HCOO⁻ = 44.998203 Da, which correctly includes the electron.

The released data is consistent with this. Fragment masses read 0.49 mDa higher in [M+H]⁺ spectra than in [M−H]⁻ spectra, and the gap is roughly the same at every m/z.

If your peak matching tolerance is 0.01 Da or more, this won't affect you. It matters more for tight fragment-formula matching. Subtracting ~0.5 mDa from positive-mode MS2 m/z values corrects it.

Could the organizers confirm whether the hidden test spectra went through the same calibration?

comments.content: Thank you for your patience on this. Tracking down which test spectra were processed with this version.
